evidence.claim: The ministry said the foundation of Akkuyu NPP Unit 4 was laid on 21 July 2022 and framed the project as advancing Türkiye's national nuclear-energy path.
evidence.title: Akkuyu NGS'nin dördüncü reaktörünün temeli atıldı
evidence.publisher: T.C. Enerji ve Tabii Kaynaklar Bakanlığı
evidence.excerpt: The ministry said the foundation of Akkuyu NPP Unit 4 was laid on 21 July 2022 and framed the project as advancing Türkiye's national nuclear-energy path.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct ministerial announcement on a dated 2022 project milestone.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Official government project milestone under Erdoğan's administration, but it is a civil-energy choice rather than a weapons-control act.
contrary_evidence: The same page also shows the project is Rosatom-led and therefore strategically dependent on Russia.

evidence.claim: Erdoğan said Türkiye could play a facilitating role on the Zaporizhzhia nuclear-plant issue and both leaders reiterated that Akkuyu should continue as planned.
evidence.title: President Erdoğan, President Putin of Russia talk over phone
evidence.publisher: Republic of Türkiye Directorate of Communications
evidence.excerpt: Erdoğan said Türkiye could play a facilitating role on the Zaporizhzhia nuclear-plant issue and both leaders reiterated that Akkuyu should continue as planned.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official presidential communications readout with a dated direct statement by Erdoğan.
contrary_evidence: A facilitation offer is not proof that he achieved an actual safety outcome at Zaporizhzhia.

evidence.claim: Erdoğan said he did not want a new Chernobyl and asked Russia to remove mines and other weapons from the Zaporizhzhia area.
evidence.title: President Erdoğan answers journalists' questions on his return flight from Ukraine
evidence.publisher: Republic of Türkiye Directorate of Communications
evidence.excerpt: Erdoğan said he did not want a new Chernobyl and asked Russia to remove mines and other weapons from the Zaporizhzhia area.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official transcript of Erdoğan's remarks with direct quotes and topic context.
contrary_evidence: The remarks show concern and mediation intent, but not direct control over the battlefield or the plant.

evidence.claim: Russia and Ukraine signed a landmark deal on 22 July 2022 to reopen Ukrainian Black Sea ports for grain exports after talks brokered by the United Nations and Turkey.
evidence.title: Ukraine, Russia sign deal to reopen grain export ports as war rages on
evidence.excerpt: Russia and Ukraine signed a landmark deal on 22 July 2022 to reopen Ukrainian Black Sea ports for grain exports after talks brokered by the United Nations and Turkey.
evidence.source_locator: search result snippet / Reuters dispatch summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reporting is independently corroborated by the official Istanbul ceremony and multiple mirrors.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong but multilateral; Erdoğan is part of the mediation, not the sole cause of the outcome.
contrary_evidence: The deal was UN-brokered and depended on both Russia and Ukraine, so it is not a unilateral Erdoğan achievement.

evidence.claim: Erdoğan said Turkey and Russia had reached a deal resolving the Akkuyu dispute and reinstating the Turkish contractor IC Ictas.
evidence.title: Turkey, Russia reach deal resolving nuclear plant dispute -Erdogan/media
evidence.excerpt: Erdoğan said Turkey and Russia had reached a deal resolving the Akkuyu dispute and reinstating the Turkish contractor IC Ictas.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters dispatch carried by Euronews with a dated quotation from Erdoğan and follow-up details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Erdoğan's management of the project, but still a negotiated outcome with Russia.
contrary_evidence: The same report shows Rosatom had terminated the contract the previous month, highlighting Türkiye's dependence on a Russian-controlled project.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 Turkish nuclear command-and-control or custody evidence is absent; the dossier mostly shows inherited treaty/NATO/IAEA posture plus civil-nuclear and mediation choices.
Direct forensic or documentary proof of Erdoğan's own assets, beneficial ownership, or personal enrichment in 2022 is still missing.
Independent corroboration beyond Reuters-style reporting is still thin for the media-control and family-access claims.
Audit-grade verification of project delivery and personnel effects is still thin; the package leans heavily on official program documents and self-reported completion counts.
